nodes.description: There is no SYCP2L-directed therapy. As for other causes of POI, estrogen with progestogen replaces ovarian hormones to limit the bone, cardiovascular and other consequences of early estrogen loss. It does not restore fertility, for which donor oocytes are the usual option. The progestogen is bound as progesterone because the ChEBI progestogen class is a role term that the agent slot does not admit. Other progestogens are used equally.

evidence.snippet: The potential implications include adverse effects on quality of life; fertility; and bone, cardiovascular and cognitive health. Although hormone therapy (HT) can mitigate some of these effects, many questions still remain regarding the optimal management of POI.

nodes.description: Without SYCP2L, oocytes still form and enter the primordial pool, but the arrested dictyate oocytes are lost faster than normal as the female ages. SYCP2L acts late in prophase I: it joins the synaptonemal complex in late diplotene and stays on the centromeres of dictyate oocytes. No synapsis or recombination defect has been reported in Sycp2l-null oocytes. What the knockout shows is faster loss of the arrested pool, not the early prophase arrest seen with most meiotic POI genes. The cause of the faster loss is not known.

nodes.description: The disease alleles remove SYCP2L or stop it reaching the centromere. Wild-type SYCP2L localizes to centromeres, both in dictyate oocytes and when expressed in somatic cells. This localization needs the C-terminal part of the protein, which the truncating alleles lack.
